verdict.tagline: Promising medieval city builder held back by shallow systems and bugs.
for_you_if: you enjoy medieval town building sandbox games
you can overlook incomplete features and placeholder assets
not_for_you_if: you need stable pathfinding and functioning worker AI
you expect deep combat and working enemy lords
you will not tolerate crashes and broken save states

distortion_flags.sentence: Recent reviews rate the game lower than lifetime reviews.

cohorts.summary: Players report bugs with pathfinding, worker tasks, and crashes alongside shallow combat and incomplete castle building features.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that workers stop performing assigned tasks, getting stuck or moving aimlessly while resources are consumed.

citations.review_text: Its good ig. But my woodcutters arent cutting wood and my communal baker building stopped working even though it should be.

Would be great if the workers didn't just stop doing stuff.. at random, like being assigned stops responding.. The mechanics and gameplay here are solid -- I consider this one of the better city builders in my library based on how intuitive the system is. However, after 7 years of early access... and especially as a developer myself -- why are devs still refining the pathfinding and balance? There is no decent upgrading past houses/artisanship, and the castle mechanics are completely empty. That part was extremely disappointing solely given how long this game has been out. 

If you are okay with a game that likely will never be in its full state, go for it when it's on sale, but I cannot recommend the full price for a game missing so much functionality. This game will be amazing if the developers finish it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system and tactical mechanics as weak, awful, or difficult to understand due to a lack of tutorials.

citations.review_text:
Not yet. Just wait, think it will be great one day.

But here is my worry, and my primary reason for leaving a negative review:

The game focuses a ton on things that are cool, but not "fun". Love the systems, and I think eventually it will all come together, probably. But wait for that, dont jump in now. City building, great! Combat? Awful. Trading; okey+

Also they had this since the start that as your city levels up you will get to "focus" it by selecting tech, so you can make your city better at trading but it comes at the cost of something else and so on. They reworked this system before and this is the newest, but atm just like before its still only for 1 level up. This is a fun system that lets you enjoy each run differently, but instead the devs chooses to spend time on logistical things that potentially makes the game more tedious. Now Im not saying thats wrong, its their game. But for me, I want to enjoy the game as well as authenticity, and that just not there yet. 

So just wait. I know its been 7 years developed. But there are true dedication here, we just gotta wait.

Several tutorials, most are helpful "ish" but not understanding if this, or every game, is meant to be a hundred year war? Lacking the tutorials for combat.... you need to actually win. Its ultimately a farm sim until combat and theres not much to help when combat commences, and your farm sim is decimated. You need a ton of livestock, it doesn't talk much about that. building upkeep? talks about even less... Is it better to just build another? It pops up red, needing addressed, and it just disappears when you scroll down to address? Disappointed.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game has a steep learning curve and lacks thorough tutorials or adequate guides for core mechanics like combat and logistics.

citations.review_text:
It has a lot of potential, but it's not anywhere near ready for its prices.

- Weak tutorial, a lot of missing explanation for different game mechanics or in-game resources.
- Not very optimized. It runs fine on my system, but I have a pretty strong PC and the game loads the GPU almost fully.
- No proper statistics/overview panel - bad for such genre of games.

There's the bones of a good game here.
Unfortunately there's no tutorial and both the UI and many game logics seem janky AF.
Can't make tax decisions while your manor's being renovated ...because the taxman needs a roof?
Got rye?  ...Can't make rye bread ....beacause your peasants are gourmets?
Kill a bunch of bandits?  ....Can't loot anything.
I dunno.
Giving it a 6.5-7 out of 10 on sheer gameplay innovation and a nice artstyle.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the castle building features and mechanics as incomplete or empty.

citations.review_text:
Not even close to being finished and its 7 years old. brilliant so far, but there's absolutely no point in buying yet unless you are REALLY REALLY REALLY interested. So far its sort of like city skyscapes or whatever that games called... but medieval... unfinished...with limited resources per map and occasional weird little bits and bugs (not many) For example: If you make a new settlement and use all of your logs or something before building everything that's absolutely integral... you are soft locked. Nothing will tell you this until you either realise yourself or see a tiny bit of text when you open a menu or something... The building is very good and fun but sometimes it can be a bit finicky, walls and gates being the wrong way round and such), AND EVEN THE CASTLE BUILDING... a KEY part of this game, maybe even the main part, is unfinished too. There are 2 buildings that are strictly just for looks and towers are so far useless. (oh one of those useless buildings is just yet to have its reason added yet...) 

Like I say, brilliant game so far... but completely unfinished (they do say literally as soon as you boot up the game tbf). I don't think you'd be able to 'complete' this game on sandbox mode yet. All of the parts just aren't there yet. Still, worth the money and time.

The mechanics and gameplay here are solid -- I consider this one of the better city builders in my library based on how intuitive the system is. However, after 7 years of early access... and especially as a developer myself -- why are devs still refining the pathfinding and balance? There is no decent upgrading past houses/artisanship, and the castle mechanics are completely empty. That part was extremely disappointing solely given how long this game has been out. 

If you are okay with a game that likely will never be in its full state, go for it when it's on sale, but I cannot recommend the full price for a game missing so much functionality. This game will be amazing if the developers finish it.

claims.claim: Tutorials and explanations for core mechanics are lacking, making the game unintuitive to learn.

citations.review_text:
This game has a long way to go.
It's not intuitive at all, tutorials and explanations are lackluster to say the least. Develplements are still unavailable, optimisation needs more work and it severely lacks decorations.
It's very incomplete.
But, this is probably the bets looking city builder I ever played, with heaps of potential and a comunicative team behind it. Should you give it a go? Yes, but understand it's not easy and lacks many things. 
It is, however, extremly good for what it has and I see it having a very bright future ahead.

I want to like this game sooooo much. I keep waiting a few months and then coming back to it to see if it has been made a little more playable but it just gets worse. If it held your hand just a tiny bit to explain basic mechanics that would be one thing but it doesn't. And then you are left trying to figure out if you are struggling with a bug or if you are just missing something and you have no way to know for sure. I spawned with a hunting area nearby and I built a hunters hut, thinking that my hunters would then go gather food resources. But they just sat there while my citizens starved. Am I missing how to assign them to the hunting area? Am I supposed to do something else to manage their priorities? Or is the game just bugged right now? I have no idea. 

The system for expanding your territory is extremely tedious. When you claim a new area, it is not treated like an expansion of your settlement, it is a brand new settlement. So now you are managing 2 DIFFERENT populations of people and having to send resources back and forth in addition to the rest of the micromanagement which doesn't work particularly well. 

I am sure that the vision for this game is amazing and maybe when it comes out of early access as a full release it will be awesome. But the development is so slow that I am afraid I have to give up on this one. It  would bring a ton of depth if the systems or mechanics were explained better but instead that depth turns into sheer complexity which is frustrating. 

I did not get this game for free. I paid for early access because this is exactly the kind of game that I love. But I would wait for the full release to buy it and hopefully its issues get sorted out.

Its a fun city builder. Can get out of hand quickly though if you dont know what youre doing or pay attention. Battling needs some work too. Telling your guys what to do on the battlefield is a pain. If game devs are looking at this, you need a help/tips box for newer players. Something that says what is recommended to build or do to keep on the right track. Also, the manor is one of the first things to be built but when you build it youre way to poor to build the fences and stuff. That needs to be something that can be accessed later or separate of the Manor. Its fun though and I enjoy it a lot.

Firewood from market is to slow. i had 2 fully manned storages(12 workers)  and 3 markets but a town of 30 houses freezes because the markets cant stock fast enough. Add a House insulation upgrade so you can upgrade houses and decrease them needing infinite firewood/coal.

Buts its also a pointless unused mechanic unless you take 20 in game years to build a wall around your entire town. The Core city mechanics need attention first.

There are so many good things about this game, but at the end of the day I paid $40 for a game that feels very unfinished. After playing about 20 hours, I don't feel like playing more until the bugs are fixed and some more content has been added. This early access at that price point is pretty steep. A few of the bugs/annoyances I encountered:

- Villagers won't use bridges - this becomes exceptionally game-breaking when you only have a single food resource in the area and it's across a river that requires a bridge to harvest it. 
- Too few resources in regions - I've played a ton of city builders/simulations like this (the most similar is Farthest Frontier) and there are many resources in even the toughest regions that makes gameplay a challenge but not completely hopeless. Especially for food. I find it a bit unrealistic and unnecessary for an entire region of forest NOT to have animals you can harvest from a hunting camp. Prioritizing food should be #1 but the game makes it impossible to have more than 1 source of food at any time (depending on seasonality) which can seriously bottleneck growth or even make it so you're required to start in a new region. 
- Farming mechanic is broken - Fertility and yield in the game seem to be broken. Planting and sowing in a fertile region seems to have little impact on the yield at all. My field fertility went from 100% to 0% in just 2 years, even though I was leaving the field farrow for 2/3 years like the tutorial recommended. I maximized bonuses, used oxen to plow, and had the maximum amount of works for the size of the farm but still only yielded about 20 wheat for a massive piece of land that took almost 2-3 years to get fully functional. Farming in the game simply requires too much effort and resources to be worth it at this point, but then you have to pray you get a good source of food from a node like the point above. 
- The above points with regards to expanding your town into a large city are almost impossible unless…

Eh, it was enjoyable at first because it kind of had this new car smell; new things that other city builders didn't have, but as time went on and the updates slowed to a trickle, it lost that smell rather quickly.  I do understand that it has a solo dev (that now has a team, btw), but to be honest, it's really just another game stuck in EA purgatory.  It eventually became boring after a certain point because it lacks any real substance in the end game.  Now granted, I haven't played it again with the last couple of update but from what I've seen, it wouldn't really change my opinion of it.

just wait until it gets better and stuff idk not enough for me lowk

The game was incredibly promising two years ago at release and the bones are still there. It has a foundation that no other medieval city (village) building game has, and I really hope for a future where I can change this review. However, for the past two years we've gotten very little content (basically just stone castles that are frankly, not all that interesting) and just rebalance after rebalance that haven't actually changed how the game feels. Every "major" update has me saying cool while reading patchnotes, and quitting again after an hour because the "improved balance" doesn't improve the fun in any meaningful way. The communication from dev(s) has steadily dropped off to the point that the CEO of the publisher stepped in, which was promising at first but has quickly also turned lackluster because it seems there's nothing to actually report from the devs. A year ago I excused the lack of content as a responsible dev (or team, it's really unclear how many people are actually working on this game) trying to lay a stronger foundation to make integrating future content easier. However, with all the "major" reworks doing basically nothing, or undoing previous major reworks, it seems to me that the dev doesn't actually know what he wants this game to be, and is chasing himself in a circle with no direction - or the worse option, which is just doing nothing. Until I see some kind of meaningful accountability for the slow progress (besides the occasional non-apologetic tweet about game development being hard) and a good explanation from the dev for why the rebalances actually matter and should be done, I cannot recommend spending money on this game.
The Dev is incredibly slow and if this gaming hasn't meaningfully been updated sense launch.

claims.claim: Expanding territory requires managing a completely separate settlement population and moving resources between them rather than seamlessly growing the existing town.

citations.review_text:
I want to like this game sooooo much. I keep waiting a few months and then coming back to it to see if it has been made a little more playable but it just gets worse. If it held your hand just a tiny bit to explain basic mechanics that would be one thing but it doesn't. And then you are left trying to figure out if you are struggling with a bug or if you are just missing something and you have no way to know for sure. I spawned with a hunting area nearby and I built a hunters hut, thinking that my hunters would then go gather food resources. But they just sat there while my citizens starved. Am I missing how to assign them to the hunting area? Am I supposed to do something else to manage their priorities? Or is the game just bugged right now? I have no idea. 

The system for expanding your territory is extremely tedious. When you claim a new area, it is not treated like an expansion of your settlement, it is a brand new settlement. So now you are managing 2 DIFFERENT populations of people and having to send resources back and forth in addition to the rest of the micromanagement which doesn't work particularly well. 

I am sure that the vision for this game is amazing and maybe when it comes out of early access as a full release it will be awesome. But the development is so slow that I am afraid I have to give up on this one. It  would bring a ton of depth if the systems or mechanics were explained better but instead that depth turns into sheer complexity which is frustrating. 

I did not get this game for free. I paid for early access because this is exactly the kind of game that I love. But I would wait for the full release to buy it and hopefully its issues get sorted out.

I want to recommend this game so much, but I just can't! (at least not in its current state) 
first off, I have had too many problems with performance and my computer struggling to keep up, even with low graphical settings. Gameplay is *so* promising, and I absolutely love the mechanics of farming. But... it all falls apart when you expand your city into the new unlockable areas. I have followed countless online guides and tried to figure things out on my own even more, but its still impossible to understand the fighting and defensive army mechanics. Its also impossible to streamline production and keep an eye on trading unless you pause often. 

But with all my gripes, I still kept playing! And that's because I have so much faith in this project. I really do think this can be one of the best city builders when its developed more!!

I currently do not recommend this game to anyone at all since the game contains a few unavoidable bugs which can cause you to lose the gametime of an entire campaign run. I ended up losing a total of 25-30 hours of gameplay out of the 50 hours i'm carrying under my belt. The rest were experimental gametime.

The game is beautiful and its great fun, but its not worth it if the game progresses to a sudden end, then realizing that all that time has been for nothing. I am tapped out. I'm going to stop playing this game until these problems has been fixed. I will recheck this in a few months. The current bugs are easily triggered. I just stopped the game during my third and final attempt. I did some online researching, and unfortunately, it seems to be a known issue, which the community has already pointed out several times. 

Bug 1. I encountered the first bug after constructing the manor (which is needed for tax, which you can use to purchase mercenaries), I farmed + spent around 320 planks in order to build walls + gates around my city, but after finishing the walls, i cannot build anything inside the walls anymore. I am able to build outside the walls, but that's useless if you play against bandits/computer, who will try to burn everything. The problem with this bug is that rebuilding the walls is the only solution, but you'd have to demolish the entire walls first, which is non-refundable, so i would have to spend another 320 planks again.

Bug 2. Then i got another bug: after building the walls, i went into castle planner and tried to extend my outer wall (i.e. making a new line attached to the current wall), but i disliked the way it looked so i tried to remove it (alt + leftclick) but since that extension automatically became part of the entire wall, deleting made me delete everything. Then the entire wall looks like a ghost/transparent. I immediately pressed cancel. Luckily, the walls are still there, but after going back into the castle planner again, the…

How is this game getting worse with updates. Things that worked before, no longer do. 
Butchers take sheep and do nothing. They butcher 3 or 4 and you have to save/load to get them moving again. Barley, malt and ale all disappear from when loading a game. Meaning you have to wait for a harvest, then malt, and then ale for the tavern to work each time you play.
Fields DO NOT regain fertility with fallow fields. Crop rotation does nothing, leave it fallow for 3 years? Nope, still 8% fertility.
Large pasture can only conain for example 50 sheep but if you make 10 tiny pasture with same space you can have 400??
 
Fish are pointless. They are only good very early game and then pointless to ever use again. Need either ocean access for larger fish pop or just up the pop in existing rivers/ponds.

Small Game area(Red animal hunting area). Just remove it and have the hunting camp production be based on your tiles wilderness rating.

Firewood from market is to slow. i had 2 fully manned storages(12 workers)  and 3 markets but a town of 30 houses freezes because the markets cant stock fast enough. Add a House insulation upgrade so you can upgrade houses and decrease them needing infinite firewood/coal.

I had this game for quite some time. There were a few improvements like the Castle. Barely an upgrade, as i cant exactly call it a castle under the most generous circumstances. Buts its also a pointless unused mechanic unless you take 20 in game years to build a wall around your entire town. The Core city mechanics need attention first.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that controlling the shape and placement of burgage plots requires fighting an unpredictable system and abusing road placement.

citations.review_text:
I’ve played a lot of colony sims over the years, so I expected something special from *Manor Lords*, especially considering all the hype around its release. Instead, I found a game that feels surprisingly mediocre.

Yes, I know it’s Early Access. I’m willing to ignore the missing features, the bugs, and the lack of balance. Those things are expected. My problem is with the core game design.

Take the burgage plot system, which is supposed to be the game's signature mechanic. Productivity depends heavily on the size and shape of each plot, so designing them is extremely important. But actually controlling that shape is frustrating. You constantly have to abuse road placement, redraw plots multiple times, and hope the game generates something usable. With only a handful of control points, you never really know what the final result will look like.

That creates a bizarre situation: the game's central mechanic technically works, but the player has very little control over it. And that's a serious problem in a colony sim. One of the fundamental principles of the genre is that construction and planning are under the player's control. The challenge should come from making good decisions—not from fighting the interface or wrestling with an unpredictable placement system.

For me, that's not an Early Access problem. That's a problem with the game's foundation.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that AI opponents fail to build beyond their first settlement, do not attack each other, and rely on infinite troop pools during combat.

citations.review_text:
The game is excellent but there is still much more room for improvement. First off, the game is beautiful and it's an excellent and challenging city builder; it took me four or five restarts until I could start building sensibly planned settlements as there's so much to lean and so many pitfalls to fall into early on. I've already logged around 100 hours of playtime in a petty short amount of time so it's definitely addicting. The only thing that's preventing me from going back and playing again and again is the AI and battle options:
1. The AI aren't clever enough to build beyond settlement one. It would be nice to actually see their settlements involve into towns alongside yours as well as have them build their own castles
2. The AI will only attack you. It would be nice if they would also attack and try to conquer each other to make the gameplay a little more dynamic
3. It would be amazing if we could get further troops such as cavalry or artillery
4. Castle building is a little pointless at the moment as battles are typically set outside; as well there's little incentive to even build your castle, let alone options to customise it when you do
5. I would really like the ability to recruit more troops, especially as the AI seem to borrow from a seemingly infinite pool. If you don't win a battle with the AI quickly they'll just keep pouring in more and more troops from nowhere while you are extremely limited and can't recruit more while you're already engaged in battle. It's pretty unfair.

If they can add or fix any of my above requests, I can be sure that I won't have any other game to play for a very long time.

The game is pretty good, even in it's current state. They are updating and making improvements but it is slow going. The game is not done by any means. The current AI opponents are broken and do not actually work. Even with that, if you just want to build a medieval city, it is pretty fun. There are some quicks and bugs still with supply chains late game but still worth a play or 5.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that when playing on older hardware with lowest detail settings, the game runs slowly and eventually crashes.

citations.review_text: I really enjoy this game! very well thought out, it is overall a masterpiece and I 100% recommend this game. I am currently playing this on a 12 year old laptop on the lowest detail and it runs slowly and eventually crashes. its worth it!

It always amazes me to see slow development speed and updates in an early access game, because if you extrapolate the speed of the updates to the state of the game when it "released" you would've thought that development started half a century ago.

I keep seeing posts and updates in the feed but every time I open the game I barely notice any difference. Maybe a re-balance here and there, maybe this micro-feature is different, changes yes... but not additions. It's like a buggy unfinished product with horrible optimization that the developer keeps "changing" hoping the next rebalance or refactor will be "the one".

What's worse is that this could be understandable if the game had a good release but that's not the case. Back in 2024 this game felt like aimless Early Access slop, and today it feels almost the same. Don't get me wrong though, it's not abandoned; it's clear the dev(s?) are working hard on it, it's just unclear if this work is producing any significant results. Whether it's a lack of vision, misguided priorities or lack of workforce is not really for me to decide.

If you buy this game, don't expect much. This is what you got, and this is likely what you'll have in five years. If the game interests you, either give it a try or watch a video on it, chances are you'll enjoy it. It's a good game. But if you think the concept is good and believe the game needs work, then... I think you'll be disappointed if you buy it.
